papers.title_in_file: Quantum Data Encoding: A Comparative Analysis of Classical-to-Quantum Mapping Techniques and Their Impact on Machine Learning Accuracy
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction (skimmed), Section 5 Experimental Results setup, results summary and limitations, Conclusion; the large results table was seen only in layout form
papers.what_it_is: An empirical study of basis, angle and amplitude quantum data encoding as a preprocessing step for classical ML classifiers on one churn dataset.

assertions.value: The authors report that quantum basis encoding gave results competitive with or better than classical PCA encoding across the classical models they tried.
quotes: Across various models, Quantum Basis Encoding consistently demonstrated competitive or superior results compared to classical encoding methods
assertions.certainty_reason: One empirical study on a single dataset; the authors' summary sentence.
assertions.reader_inference: The layout text of the results table shows several rows where the classical accuracy figure is above the quantum basis or angle encoding figure, so the summary sentence may not hold row by row. The reader did not reconcile the table with the summary.

assertions.value: The authors state the experiments used one telecommunications customer churn dataset with 7,043 customers, undersampled to 3,738 records because of simulator limits.
quotes: passes a total of 7,043 distinct customers. This dataset is available on the Kaggle website.
performed undersampling on the majority classes, resulting in a total of 3,738 records
Due to the limitations of the simulator in handling large volumes of data
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own experimental setup, Section 5, p.7.

assertions.value: The authors report that quantum encoding added running-time overhead, modest for logistic regression and k-nearest neighbors and more noticeable for support vector machines.
quotes: the increase in running time was generally modest
more computationally intensive models like Support Vector Machines (SVM) experienced a more noticeable increase in processing time
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the study did not explore all possible machine learning algorithms and quantum encoding techniques, which limits how far the findings generalize.
quotes: machine learning algorithms and quantum encoding techniques, limiting the generalizability of the findings to the specific methods investigated.
Additionally, the dataset characteristics and quantum computing hardware used may impact the observed results
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own limitations paragraph, Section 5, p.15-16.

papers.title_in_file: A Quantum Bagging Algorithm with Unsupervised Base Learners for Label Corrupted Datasets
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction (first part), Section 4 results discussion (4.3, 4.4, Table 2) and Conclusion; method sections skimmed only
papers.what_it_is: A proposed quantum bagging framework using QMeans clustering as base learner, evaluated in simulation on small classification and regression datasets with label noise.

assertions.value: The authors report that in simulations the quantum bagging algorithm performed comparably to classical bagging with KMeans and was more resilient to label corruption than supervised bagging.
quotes: performs comparably to its classical counterpart using KMeans while exhibiting greater resilience to label corruption than supervised bagging methods
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation results on small datasets, from the abstract.
assertions.reader_inference: The base learner distance and assignment steps run classically, so the comparison is between two classical-hardware computations of a quantum-structured algorithm.

assertions.value: The authors report that under 5% label noise on the Iris, Breast Cancer and Wine datasets, bagging with unsupervised base learners (classical and quantum) outperformed bagging with supervised decision trees.
quotes: under a 5% label noise setting across the Iris, Breast Cancer, and Wine datasets. The results highlight that both classical and quantum bagging with unsupervised learner consistently outperform their supervised counterparts in noisy environments
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study; accuracy values are in Table 2.

assertions.value: The authors state that in their implementation the distance evaluation and cluster assignment steps are executed on classical hardware because of limited qubit count and noise sensitivity.
quotes: both the distance evaluation and cluster assignment phases are executed on classical hardware, while preserving the algorithmic structure that would allow for quantum subroutines in future realizations
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of how the implementation was run, Section 4.3, p.15.

papers.title_in_file: A Full Quantum Generative Adversarial Network Model for High Energy Physics Simulations
papers.what_it_is: A small prototype fully quantum GAN, simulated, that generates eight-pixel calorimeter shower images and is compared with hybrid GANs with classical discriminators.

assertions.value: The authors report that the full quantum GAN reproduced the average shower image of the Geant4 test set.
quotes: the full qGAN model can accurately reproduce the average shower image of Geant4
assertions.certainty_reason: Single prototype result in simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that a quantum discriminator with 20 trainable parameters performed about as well as a classical neural network discriminator with more than 400 trainable parameters.
quotes: the MERA-down discriminator quantum circuit architecture with only 20 trainable parameters performs equally well to a classical neural network with more than 400 trainable parameters
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical comparison within the stated statistics, Section 4.2.
assertions.reader_inference: The authors also say the accuracies are similar only within the given statistics, so a parameter-efficiency conclusion is not established by this single comparison.

assertions.value: The authors state that all experiments were run on quantum simulators and that the full quantum GAN was developed and trained as a proof of concept.
quotes: All experiments in this paper are conducted using quantum simulators.
a full qGAN model was developed and trained as a proof of concept
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup, Section 3 and Section 5.

assertions.value: The authors state that neither the full quantum GAN nor the hybrid GAN could reproduce more sophisticated physics accuracy metrics beyond the average shower image, such as pixel-wise correlation patterns.
quotes: It should be noted that both the full qGAN and the hybrid qGAN models are unable to reproduce the more sophisticated physics accuracy metrics beside the average shower image
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own stated limit, Section 4.2.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Radio Astronomy: Quantum Linear Solvers for Redundant Baseline Calibration
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Sections 5 and 6 (results, ideal and realistic settings) and Section 7 Conclusion; Appendices not read. Two-column layout interleaves in pdftotext, so some passages were read in fragments
papers.what_it_is: A study of variational quantum linear solvers and quantum-annealer QUBO solvers inside the HERA radio telescope redundancy calibration pipeline, in simulation with ideal and noisy models.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that with currently available hardware no tangible quantum advantage can be identified for this calibration task.
quotes: We therefore conclude that, at least with the hardware currently available, no tangible quantum advantage can be identified.
assertions.certainty_reason: Conclusion of one simulation study, Section 7.

assertions.value: The authors report that under ideal conditions, without limits on qubit connectivity or coherence time, both quantum linear solvers are viable alternatives for the initial loop of redundancy calibration.
quotes: both investigated quantum linear solvers are viable
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulated ideal-case results, Section 5 and Section 7.

assertions.value: The authors state that the annealer approach requires a very large number of physical qubits to compensate for the limited inter-qubit connectivity of real devices.
quotes: require a very large number of physical
qubits to compensate for the limited inter-qubit connectivity
assertions.certainty_reason: Embedding analysis in Section 6.2 and conclusion, Section 7.

assertions.value: The authors state that the realistic-setting VQLS results used a simulated noise model of the IBM Guadalupe chip, not a physical quantum computer.
quotes: We have used the noise model of the IBM Guadalupe,
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup, Section 6.1.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Ensembling Methods for Healthcare and Life Science
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, I Introduction, III Results (D datasets and A classifier performance), IV Analysis, V Conclusions; II Methods skimmed
papers.what_it_is: An empirical study of quantum ensemble classifiers on small synthetic data and renal cell carcinoma gene expression data, in simulation and on IBM hardware.

assertions.value: The authors report that on the renal cell carcinoma data the quantum classifiers showed similar to slightly improved F1 and accuracy compared with random forest, not significant except for the bagging variational classifier (p = 0.018 by t-test) on the full dataset.
quotes: the quantum classifiers showed similar to slightly improved F1 and accuracy scores as compared to the RF, though the margin does not rise to significance
whose F1 score was significantly higher than RF (p = 0.018 by t-test) when testing on the full RCC dataset
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on one dataset of 150 samples, Section III.A.
assertions.reader_inference: The t-test is over repeated train/test splits of one small dataset; splits share samples, so the p-value overstates independence.

assertions.value: The authors report that a 56 qubit quantum ensemble classifier run on an IBM Eagle processor, with minimal error mitigation and 8 training samples, reached Brier scores comparable to random forests.
quotes: Our initial experiments deploying a 56 qubit QEC on an Eagle IBM QPU (Fig. 4), demonstrates that with minimal error mitigation and with only 8 training samples, the QEC reached Brier scores comparable to random forests
assertions.certainty_reason: Initial hardware experiment, Section V and Fig. 4.

assertions.value: The authors state that the real data were gene expression counts for 150 patient samples and the synthetic benchmark used 100 labeled samples per blob configuration.
quotes: we use DESeq2 [36] to normalize RNA-seq mRNA counts for 150 patient samples
The blob datasets contain 100 labeled samples and 10 unique 80/20 train/test splits are generated
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own datasets, Section III.D.

assertions.value: The authors state that the trained variational ensembles were not deployed on hardware, leaving the quantum resources each ensemble needs as an open question.
quotes: The trained variational ensembles were not deployed on hardware, and this poses an open question about the number of quantum resources each ensemble needs.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own stated limit, Section IV.B.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Machine Learning for Energy-Efficient 5G-Enabled IoMT Healthcare Systems: Enhancing Data Security and Processing
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section II methodology (summary), Section III results text and Section IV Discussion and Conclusion; algorithm listings and figures not read in detail
papers.what_it_is: A proposal and simulated evaluation of three quantum classification algorithms (UU-dagger, variational UU-dagger and UU-dagger-QNN) on four 5G and IoMT datasets with noise models.

assertions.value: The authors report that their UU-QNN method outperformed the other two quantum algorithms on the 5G-South Asia and WUSTL EHMS 2020 datasets, achieving 100% accuracy.
quotes: outperforms the other algorithms in the 5G-South Asia and WUSTL EHMS 2020 datasets, achieving 100% accuracy
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulated empirical result, abstract and Section IV.
assertions.reader_inference: The QNN loss was computed on 10 data points per dataset, so 100% accuracy rests on a very small evaluation sample.

assertions.value: The authors state that the QNN loss was computed on 10 data points from each dataset and that the algorithms ran on the IBM QASM simulator with 1000 shots.
quotes: iteratively calculates the loss function for 10 data points from each dataset
The proposed quantum algorithms were implemented using the IBM QASM simulator with 1000 shots.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup, Section III.

assertions.value: The authors report that accuracy of the QNN stayed at 20% on the L5G1.0 dataset and state this shows a need for improved encoding, error mitigation and optimization for complex, noisy, imbalanced real-world data.
quotes: for L5G1.0, it stays at 20%
highlights the need for improved encoding, error mitigation, and more effective optimization to handle complex, noisy, and imbalanced real-world data
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result in simulation, Section III.

assertions.value: The authors state that decoherence, hardware infidelities and qubit topology limitations challenge practical deployment on current quantum hardware, and that variational training suffers from barren plateaus.
quotes: decoherence, hardware infidelities, and qubit topology limitations challenge practical deployment on current quantum hardware. Furthermore, variational training suffers from barren plateaus
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own stated limit, Section IV.

papers.title_in_file: Accelerated VQE: Parameter Recycling for Similar Recurring Problem Instances
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, Introduction, Section 5 Accelerated VQE results, Section 6 Discussion and Limitations, Section 7 Conclusion; Sections 2 to 4 skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study of transfer learning (reusing trained circuit parameters) to speed up VQE on 12 node MaxCut instances.

assertions.value: The authors report that transfer learning reduced training time by around 93% in post-training relative to identical circuits without transfer learning.
quotes: Our experiments demonstrate that transfer learning can reduce training time by around 93% in post-training
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on one problem class, abstract.

assertions.value: The authors state the approach was tested on the MaxCut problem with a problem size of 12 nodes.
quotes: tested on the MaxCut problem with a problem size of 12 nodes solved with two different circuits utilised
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope, abstract.

assertions.value: The authors report that, with a reduced iteration limit, the transfer learning approach outperformed standard initialization in 55.8% of 700 instances, matched it in 15.6% and under-performed in 28.6%.
quotes: Across all 700 instances solved, in an instance by instance comparison, the TL approach outperforms the classical training variant in 55.8% of all instances, achieves comparable results in 15.6%, and under-performs in 28.6% of all instances
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result, Section 5.
assertions.reader_inference: The authors say approximation quality at the reduced iteration limit is significantly lower than at full convergence, so the advantage is in an early-stopped regime.

assertions.value: The authors state that the study does not thoroughly examine scalability because the problem sizes tested were limited, and that the gap between source and target graphs may lead to suboptimal local minima.
quotes: our study does not thoroughly examine scalability due to the limited problem sizes tested, and the gap between source and target graphs remains a concern, as it may lead to suboptimal local minima
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own stated limit, Section 6.2.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum autoencoders for efficient compression of quantum data
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, I Introduction, II Quantum Autoencoder Model (opening), results text around Table II, V Discussion; circuit and cost-function derivation sections skimmed
papers.what_it_is: The paper that introduces a quantum autoencoder, a parameterized circuit trained classically to compress sets of quantum states, with simulated examples on Hubbard model and H4 ground states.

assertions.value: The authors introduce a quantum autoencoder trained, with classical optimization, to compress a particular dataset of quantum states.
quotes: The quantum autoencoder is trained to compress a particular dataset of quantum states, where a classical compression algorithm cannot be employed.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's definition of its own model, abstract and Section II.

assertions.value: The authors report that ground states of the two-sites Hubbard model could be compressed from 4 to 3 qubits using both circuit types, while for the 4-sites Hubbard model neither circuit model reached the error threshold they used.
quotes: We observe that the ground states of the two-sites Hubbard model can be compressed from 4 to 3 qubits using both circuit types.
In the case of the 4-sites Hubbard model, none of the circuit models proposed here was able to obtain errors below
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulated results on small systems, Section IV and Table II.

assertions.value: The authors state that the maximum rate of lossless compression is predetermined by the size of the subspace spanning the training set, so a given set of states might admit only a small or null compression rate.
quotes: the maximum rate of lossless compression achievable with a quantum autoencoder is predetermined by the size of the subspace spanning the
a given set of states might only admit a small or null compression rate
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own stated limit, Section IV, p.8.

assertions.value: The authors state that any complexity result for their construction would depend on the family of unitaries chosen for the learning, so they give no general complexity statement.
quotes: For our construction, it is clear that any complexity result would be dependent upon the family of unitaries that is chosen for the learning to be optimized over.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own stated limit, Section V.
